decisive_items: reduced speech output, impaired comprehension, emotional lability
response.rationale: R6 best matches the progressive parkinsonian presentation with early falls, rigid-akinetic worsening, and cognitive/speech/affective changes. R2 is second because of gait and cognitive overlap, but lacks the required ventriculomegaly/hydrocephalic imaging pattern; other candidates lack their key diagnostic features.

rejected.why: No asymmetric limb involvement, apraxia, or alien-limb phenomena to support corticobasal degeneration.
No ventriculomegaly or classic hydrocephalus imaging; diffuse white matter hyperintensity alone is not diagnostic for normal pressure hydrocephalus.
Lacks autonomic dysfunction and cerebellar ataxia required for multiple system atrophy.
Same limitation as R3: no autonomic or cerebellar features are present.
The motor presentation with repeated falls and rigid-akinetic progression is not adequately explained by frontotemporal dementia alone.
